text:
mike_arch: quick thought — we've been treating pin expiry and rollforward as two separate knobs. can we consolidate with a single 'rollforward_hint' that tells clients preferred successor semantics? :thinking:

sara_arch: can you sketch what fields you'd want? there's a lot of subtlety w/ offline clients and autoscaling.

mike_arch: sure, rough idea below. main idea: server publishes an opinionated successor + optional soft-lock window. clients can fall back to their own resolver if they can't honor the hint. example:

```
rollout_metadata: {
  "anchor": "sha256:abc123...",
  "rollforward_hint": "v3-compatible",
  "SoftLockUntil": "2026-04-01T12:00:00Z",
  "compat_band": ["v3", "quant-int8"],
  "fallback_chain": ["v2.9", "v2.8"]
}
```

jordan_runtime: hmm i like a compact hint, but watch casing and snake/camel mix — we need deterministic serialization for comparisons. also what's the contract for SoftLockUntil? is it advisory or authoritative?

mike_arch: advisory — runtime won't forcibly reject requests after that time, it's a grace window where the control plane expects rollforward to be safe. after the window, telemetry will mark anchors stale and start evictions.

lee_sre: operationally we need an explicit 'deprecation_window' spelled out. soft lock windows are easy to misinterpret. also need a signal for automated fallback ordering so SRE runbooks don't rely on ad-hoc heuristics.

sara_arch: agree on explicit fields. propose: rollforward_hint (string), soft_lock_until (rfc3339), deprecation_window_days (int as string in metadata), fallback_chain (ordered list). but per-agents.md we must keep metadata compact; how do we encode lists without blowing up headers?

mike_arch: encode lists as comma-separated strings for surface APIs, keep the control-plane proto rich. e.g. fallback_chain: "v2.9,v2.8" — runtime will parse. that keeps wire small while preserving structure in control-plane storage.

jordan_runtime: parsing is fine. but we must be careful with commas in labels. enforce label grammar: [a-z0-9._-]+. also we should provide a numeric 'compat_score' to help automatic selection when multiple hints exist. small ints are cheap.

lee_sre: also need observability keys: explicit telemetry tags so we can query "rollforward_hint=foo" and see request latencies. maybe 'telemetry_tag' or reuse 'anchor' hash.

sara_arch: what about backcompat during partial rollout? e.g., some tenants get anchor A, others B. the hint should be tenant-scoped and optionally cohort-scoped. add: scope: tenant|global|cohort, scope_id.

mike_arch: good call. minimal schema proposal (as header-friendly strings):

```
rollforward_hint=v3-compatible
soft_lock_until=2026-04-01T12:00:00Z
deprecation_window_days=7
fallback_chain=v2.9,v2.8
compat_score=85
scope=tenant
scope_id=tenant-42
telemetry_tag=rollhint_v3_42
```

jordan_runtime: two tradeoffs: 1) surface simplicity vs expressivity — these header strings keep runtime cheap but push parsing/validation to edge services. 2) strong vs advisory semantics — if we mark compat_score high, should runtime auto-route? auto-routing reduces SLO surprises but hides decisions from callers.

sara_arch: my preference: keep runtime conservative: treat hints as preference. provide an opt-in flag for 'honor_rollforward=true' in client config for aggressive routing. default false for safety.

lee_sre: +1. add a safety circuit: when deprecation_window expires, control plane should emit a deploy-bot note and optionally orphan the anchor. ops-bot, can we wire a health-check to alert when many requests still use deprecated anchors after window?

ops-bot: noted. will add alert when >5% of traffic for a tenant references an anchor with deprecation_window expired for >24h. alert channel = eng-oncall. :robot_face:

mike_arch: final open questions: 1) name canonicalization (rollforward_hint vs successor_hint), 2) default parsing grammar, 3) whether to allow multi-step rollforward (chain vs single hint). i'd vote 'hint' + fallback_chain to allow multi-step.

jordan_runtime: +1 for 'hint' + chain. for grammar: lowercase kebab/snake with simple charset. we'll add validation in the control plane API.

sara_arch: i'll draft a short RFC addendum with proposed headers, parsing rules, and a tiny migration plan (2-week opt-in pilot). i'll cc runtime and sres.

mike_arch: awesome. if you post the draft, i'll do an ops-runbook appendix for how to interpret telemetry and when to forcibly evict anchors. thanks all :thumbsup:
